order_X.lesson: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.

order_Y.verse line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
Worry grows when you feed it thought, like fire with fuel. Starve it, and it dies down.

order_Y.reference: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
order_Y.verse line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
A pot draws the same water from a well or the ocean. Keep your dignity before the rich.
Feed people, find water for animals; when even ants live off your home, you become a world for them.
Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.

order_X.verse line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
I understand your advice perfectly. My heart still isn't at peace.
You torment yourself with shame for nothing. In my eyes you stand above them all.
Don't punish the whole world for one person's wrong.
Learn everything that is good from others, but bring it in, and in your own way absorb it; do not become others.
Envy is an itch. Burning at another's happiness is a wasting disease of the mind.

order_X.summary: Seeing Bharat's army approach the Ganga, Guha assumes he is coming to kill Ram and prepares his men to die fighting. An old man reads the omens and says Bharat comes to bring Ram back. Guha agrees that fools act in haste and repent, goes to meet Bharat with gifts, and the two embrace.
order_X.lesson: Find out someone's intent before you prepare for war with them.

Start the day by greeting your mother and father. Small daily respect adds up to a good life.
Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.

Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
The Lord is hidden in your own heart. By his grace one sees him, and sorrow lifts.

Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.

order_X.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

Inwardly hand all your work to the divine, hold it as your goal, and keep your mind on it.

order_X.lesson: Honesty about who you are is the best credential you can bring.

order_X.verse line: So keep doing the work that needs doing, well and without clinging. That's how you rise.
A good mind doesn't leave what is right, though a million obstacles come.
Without understanding, the senses bolt like wild horses; with a steady mind, they run like trained ones.
Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
Every result is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some don't. Those who never try never do.
Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.

order_X.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
order_X.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.
